title: Renewal: SLO tiering & capacity reservation options
text:
Renewal: SLO tiering & capacity reservation options

['From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Toliver <sam.toliver@amplitech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal planning — SLO tiers, capacity reservation options

Hi Sam —

As we approach your annual renewal (RDW-DEAL-78412), I wanted to propose a structure that aligns AmpliTech’s performance needs with predictable economics. Based on the traffic profile you shared, the two levers that will move the needle are: a) SLO tiering for tail-latency guarantees (p50/p95/p99 bands) and b) a capacity reservation with burst headroom.

Key proposal (high level):
- Premium SLO Tier: 30ms p50 / 120ms p95 / 400ms p99 for inference on your core routing (applies to text-gen and chat routes).
- Reserved Capacity: 8 reserved GPU units guaranteed for baseline throughput + 50% burst pool for spiky days.
- Support: 24x7 priority support with dedicated escalation line and 16 SE hours/quarter for runbooks & run-rate tuning.
- Term: 12-month renewal with an option to extend to 24 months at a 6% discount on the reserved capacity line item.
- Credits: Service credits tied to missed p99 windows (tiered; small SLA credit at p99 miss, larger credit if repeated across a month).

I’ve attached a short SLA tiering doc and a preliminary capacity quote. If you’re open, would like to book 30 minutes next week to walk through the numbers and the operational handoff (on-call, runbook, canary rollout)?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference

', 'From: Sam Toliver <sam.toliver@amplitech.com>

Cc: Priya Sharma <psharma@amplitech.com>, AmpliTech Procurement <procurement@amplitech.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — SLO tiers, capacity reservation options

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear start. A few questions from our side before we sync with procurement:
1) Can you define the credit calculation for p99 misses? We need an example (monthly traffic baseline -> credit %).
2) For the burst pool, will burst capacity incur additional overage charges beyond the reserved line item?
3) The SE hours — can those be used for on-site runbook workshops or limited to remote ops?

I’m copying Priya (Ops) and procurement so we can get pricing and legal visibility. We’d like to understand whether a 12 or 24 month term is more favorable cost-wise and any flexibility on phased ramping of reservations.

Best,
Sam
Head of Platform — AmpliTech
', 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <psharma@amplitech.com>, Sam Toliver <sam.toliver@amplitech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-04T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — SLO tiers, capacity reservation options

Hi Priya / Sam —

Good questions — quick answers inline, and I’ve attached the worked example in the quote spreadsheet: see the "SLA credit examples" tab.

1) Credit calc: If p99 > promised threshold for more than 0.5% of requests in a monthly window, we issue a pro-rated credit on the reserved capacity line. Example: baseline monthly spend on reserved capacity = $120,000. Single-month p99 breach (one event covering >0.5% of requests) = 10% credit on reserved capacity = $12,000. Repeated breaches (>=3 distinct weekly events) escalate to 25% credit for the month. Full details in doc.

2) Burst accounting: Burst capacity is included up to the 50% pool for short durations (first 6 minutes per burst session). Sustained usage beyond burst -> billed at overage rate (lower than on-demand). We can cap monthly overage exposure in the contract.

3) SE hours: Convertible — up to 8 hours/quarter can be used on-site for workshops; remainder remote. We’ll formalize SOW in the renewal addendum.

If this looks OK, Marissa (CC) can share the formal quote and Ben can provide an ops checklist for the handoff. Do you have availability Wed 12/6 or Thu 12/7 for a 30-min call?

Thanks —
Karthik

', 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-06T09:42:00Z
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — SLO tiers, capacity reservation options

Hi Priya / Sam —

Following up with a formal quote + a short appendix that captures the SLO bands and credit tables (attached). A few notes from a commercial/legal perspective:
- We can include a monthly overage cap to provide predictability; suggest starting at 15% of reserved spend and revisiting after the first quarter.
- For a 24-month term we can apply a 6% discount on the reserved capacity line and include an SLA performance bonus (credit threshold moved tighter by 10% after the first year if both parties agree).
- DocuSign envelope is attached for the renewal addendum; legal redlines should come back within 5 business days to keep the 12/31 renewal effective date.

Operational ask: Ben (copy) will run the pre-rollout checklist — we need AmpliTech to confirm the three test routes for canary traffic, provide a short-term traffic replay window, and validate prefix cache hit expectations.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference

', "From: Priya Sharma <psharma@amplitech.com>

Date: 2028-12-15T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — SLO tiers, capacity reservation options

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the thorough materials and the call yesterday. Procurement has reviewed the DocuSign and a few minor legal items are being clarified (data residency clause and overage cap language). We are comfortable moving forward with the following agreed items:
- 12-month term starting 2029-01-01
- Reserved Capacity: 8 units baseline + 50% burst pool
- Premium SLO Tier applied to main inference routes (p50/p95/p99 as noted)
- 16 SE hours/quarter (8 on-site convertible)
- Monthly overage cap: 15% of reserved capacity spend

Please route the final DocuSign to procurement once legal redlines are incorporated. Ben / Grace — we’re ready to schedule the pre-rollout checklist run (traffic replay window) and a 60-minute runbook workshop the week of 1/8.

Regards,
Priya Sharma
VP, Platform Engineering — AmpliTech
